messages:
anna: seeing a sudden 38% drop in GPU capacity in ap-southeast-1 — huge queue growth on inference workers, started ~08:10 UTC :rotating_light:
ops-bot: ALERT: cluster-gpu-ap-southeast1 - host_evictions spike (past 10m) - 42 hosts lost - affected pools: inference,gpu-burst
netmon-bot: NET: connectivity flaps detected to provider edge in ap-southeast-1, some pods report RTOs, TCP retransmit surge
raj: is this spot/preemptible eviction or underlying network? can we get host-level events?
anna: cloud provider reported spot reclaiming in the region + some networking instability. majority of evicted instances were spot.
linda: recommend: 1) pause autoscaler from launching more spot instances; 2) kick over to on-demand fallback for critical pools; 3) apply per-customer soft caps to stabilize queues
kevin: agreed. applying soft caps now for non-enterprise tiers. intend to limit per-customer concurrent tokens to ~0.6 qps for free, 3 qps for standard while we stabilize.
kevin: config snippet I'm going to push to rate-limit service:
```
POST /admin/rate-limits/override
{
  "scope": "per_customer",
  "overrides": [
    {"tier": "free", "qps": "0.6"},
    {"tier": "standard", "qps": "3"}
  ],
  "reason": "ap-southeast-1 spot eviction - emergency soft caps"
}
```
anna: who can execute that POST? I don't want a manual mistake during the incident.
sam: i can run it now. pushing via admin with dry-run then apply.
deploy-bot: change request created: CR-4567 - "Emergency per-customer soft caps (ap-southeast-1)" by sam
sam: executing:
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"scope":"per_customer","overrides":[{"tier":"free","qps":"0.6"},{"tier":"standard","qps":"3"}],"reason":"evictions"}' https://ops-api.redwood.internal/admin/rate-limits/override
```
sam: applied override and enabled propagate=true. returning status: 202 Accepted.
anna: queue depth on inference-router dropped ~45% within 2m of the change, CLS latency spike reduced. great. :thumbsup:
raj: can we route paid traffic to eu-west1 as a temporary failover for high-paying customers? will need routing policy update and customer opt-in maybe for latency-sensitive apps.
linda: we have a policy for tiered failover — need approvals but we can do per-customer reroute for enterprise customers. opening runbook step: RB-98 -> traffic-reshuffle.
kevin: keep an eye on cost — on-demand and cross-region egress will increase spend. track burn to the incident cost bucket.
anna: i've notified account-ops for impacted customers and PR/CS for external comms.
sam: autoscaler set to avoid spot launches, on-demand pool expanding (2x target) — monitoring host stabilization.
anna: next steps: (1) keep soft caps in place until region stable (2) continue on-demand ramp (3) re-evaluate in 60m and decide rollback or continue reroute for enterprise. filing incident follow-up ticket I-2026 and assigning infra.
linda: noted, assigning to infra-team and tagging for postmortem.
anna: thanks all — will update in 20.
ops-bot: Incident I-2026 created and attached to CR-4567 for tracking."
